submission.justification: Absorber-F1 at 5 mm gives the best simulated energy resolution for 100 GeV electrons: 3.10% (100k events). Nearby points were 4 mm 3.19%, 4.5 mm 3.22%, 5.5 mm 3.29%, 6 mm 3.12%, so the optimum is roughly 5-6 mm and the scan is slightly noisy. F2 at its best (5 mm) gave 3.79% and F3 at its best (5 mm) gave 5.12%. The 2025 summary is consistent with this ranking. The hard dose-rate constraint (<= 20 uSv/h at 1 m after one week of cooldown) could NOT be verified: no project document contains activation or dose data, and the simulation tool only returns resolution. This recommendation is therefore conditional. F1 must not be adopted until an activation calculation confirms the dose limit. If F1 fails that check, the next choice is F2 at 5 mm (3.79%), and only if both fail, F3 at 5 mm (5.12%), which is a standard structural absorber and is probably the lowest-activation option but has not been checked either. Cooling (18 C water, electronics-dominated heat load), readout (common to all options) and mechanical support (compatible with all candidates) do not discriminate between the materials.

requirements.requirement: Absorber must be one of the three candidate materials
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F1 is one of the three options in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: Best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F1 at 5 mm gave 3.10%, the best of all scanned points (F2 best 3.79% at 5 mm; F3 best 5.12% at 5 mm). Scan points 4-6 mm for F1 were 3.12-3.29%, so the optimum is around 5-6 mm.

requirements.requirement: Residual dose rate at 1 m after one week cooldown <= 20 uSv/h (hard requirement)
requirements.evidence: No document in the project contains activation or dose-rate data for any candidate, and the simulation tool does not report it. Compliance for F1 at 5 mm is unverified. This is a blocking item that must be checked before adoption.
